tier_reason: ReadMe.md says segregated heaps 'beat the original bmalloc at object churn performance' and that libpas 'achieves much better memory usage than bmalloc' because it returns pages sooner, with no numbers or methodology.
notes: Kept at D despite no numbers because libpas is widely deployed (WebKit/Safari/JSC). BSD-2-Clause confirmed from the Apple copyright header in src/libpas/pas_heap.h. Repo id is the whole WebKit monorepo; libpas lives in Source/bmalloc/libpas.

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed OOPSLA 2024 paper (Effect Handlers for C via Coroutines) evaluates libseff against libco and cppcoro; bench/context_switch_bench has libseff.cpp, libco.cpp and cppcoro.cpp, but the paper (with compiler/flags) could only be read via search snippets, so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Per search snippets of the OOPSLA 2024 paper (PDF blocked): generator benchmark libseff 0.66 us vs libco 1.33 us, about 2x faster than libco and 1.7x faster than cppcoro; libseff consistently fastest among effect-handler libraries. Snippet only.
corrections.caveats: Snippet only: the paper PDF (dl.acm.org, homepages.inf.ed.ac.uk, pure-oai.bham.ac.uk) is blocked here, so numbers vs libco come from search snippets; paper also notes the hot-split problem makes a call to an empty function 11x slower than a plain C call under segmented stacks. bench/ vendors libco, cppcoro, libmprompt, libhandler and cpp-effects as git submodules. Mulan PSL v2 is OSI-approved. Low star count (16). Last commit 2025-07-09, over 12 months ago.

notes: Downgrade of maintenance to stale (last commit 2025-07-09 vs today 2026-10). Tier B rests on the peer-reviewed paper; a retier to A is possible if the paper's methodology section (compiler, flags, CPU) becomes reachable.

tier_reason: First-party doc/benchmarks.adoc gives timings vs asio::awaitable and asio stackful (Boost.Context) coroutines on an i7-1185G7 with gcc 12 / clang 16, but no compiler flags, so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: posting 50M times: cobalt 2472 ms gcc12 / 2098 ms clang16 vs stackful 3655 / 3725 ms (about 1.5x-1.8x, derived from page data), awaitable 2432 / 2253 ms; parallel zero-size channel 3M: cobalt 1563 / 1468 ms vs awaitable 2800 / 2805 ms (no stackful row); immediate channel 10M: cobalt 1810 / 1864 ms vs awaitable 3109 / 4110 and stackful 3922 / 4705 ms; cobalt::channel 3M: 500 / 350 ms vs awaitable 790 / 770 and stackful 867 / 907 ms
